scientific_decisions.source_name: Proposal to replace canonical Limnodea arkansana with Graphephorum arkansanum solely because a 2024 combination exists
scientific_decisions.reason: POWO/WCVP continues to accept Limnodea; Fu's broader genus concept is not adopted by the project backbone. Preserve the alternative name as a synonym with concept caution.

scientific_decisions.source_name: Proposal to create additional accepted learner cards for Greenia arkansana, Cinna arkansana, or Graphephorum arkansanum
scientific_decisions.reason: These are homotypic names for the same type under the current backbone; separate canonical cards would duplicate one taxon concept.

scientific_decisions.source_name: Species-level identity of individual source photographs or historical vouchers labelled Ozarkgrass
scientific_decisions.reason: An accepted taxon name and historic synonym mappings do not independently authenticate an individual photographed plant or an ambiguous specimen. Preserve existing photo/identity review status; do not infer hybrid origin.

scientific_decisions.source_name: Alternative generic circumscription: Limnodea versus Graphephorum
scientific_decisions.accepted_target: POWO/WCVP: Limnodea arkansana; Fu (2024): Graphephorum arkansanum
scientific_decisions.reason: Fu proposed synonymizing Limnodea into Graphephorum, whereas POWO/WCVP retains Limnodea; Barberá et al. (2024) treated Limnodea separately and reported monophyly in their sampled trees. Accepted backbone is clear, broader taxonomic disagreement remains.

scientific_decisions.source_name: Historical records labelled only Greenia, Thurberia, Limnas, or 'Ozark grass' without voucher/author
scientific_decisions.reason: Incomplete generic or vernacular labels cannot establish exact identity or authorship. Keep these records unassigned until original determination and voucher are checked.

follow_up: Preserve current Limnodea learner name and its specimen-ID holds; optionally hand off authorship to authorized card worker. Do not treat Fu's Graphephorum combination as an accepted second species or assume photos authenticated by synonymy.
